execution_amendment: Two pre-report runs exposed that alpha=0 cannot preserve source-relative channel boundaries when mapped luminance itself lies in the boundary region. The evaluator was corrected to report this frozen-gate failure instead of raising before evidence; the operator, inputs, thresholds and metrics were unchanged.
interpretation: The factorization retains exact target luminance, low gradient inversion, strong visible separation and a population median chroma scale of one.
For dark or channel-extreme pixels, target luminance alone can enter a new source-relative boundary; reducing AO6 chroma cannot repair this, and five rows also require substantial chroma attenuation.
The exact zero-luminance AO6 chroma substitution is therefore structurally incompatible with the frozen boundary contract on this development population.
next_action: Retain AO6 and close this exact factorization. A successor must preserve the already-safe CB11 chroma base and add only a continuously bounded AO6-relative chroma residual, rather than scaling AO6 chroma from zero.
claim_ceiling: Closed development-only factorization on consumed CC0 display proxies; not a negative result about AO6, CB11 luminance, calibrated film response or all bounded chroma-residual mechanisms.
